title: Leaderboard high-score quote discrepancy
detail: The session brief states 0.3195 is the highest current score. The family's stored, dated read of the official leaderboard (GEMSDOE32 docs/sources, 2026-10-04) records #1 nchuzhoy 0.3262, #2 DARD 0.3195, #3 alexoktaba 0.3042. Either the board changed between 2026-10-04 and the brief, or ranks were transposed.
action: Do not quote either number as current without a fresh read of https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/leaderboard/. Both values on this site are dated and sourced.

title: UCD Fault Analysis Group TSG-2008 abstract URL not machine-verified
detail: The lane brief cites a UCD Fault Analysis Group TSG-2008 abstract for >=100-200 m DEM truncation of mapped fault tips. The exact abstract URL could not be verified from this sandbox (egress restricted). The research page marks the claim pending manual verification; the independent Southampton eprint 76146 citation covers the same mechanism (~500 m tip under-mapping).
action: Manual verification of the TSG-2008 abstract URL before the claim is used in any scored argument.

title: Halo-saturated witness degeneracy in the literal 70% forward-overlap rule
detail: The final-dot check fires literally against gems61-lane-buried-step-gravinversion-hgm-r3-k400k-b2zeros.tif (311,617 dots; 3 px halo covers 96.96% of allowed cells; chance-expected forward overlap 0.9696). Control measurement: the ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED 0.2778 incumbent (h33-2-b2) trips the same test at 0.987 forward overlap with Jaccard 0.0069. The rule therefore cannot discriminate lane drift for any evidence-placed candidate. Precedent: GEMSDOE65 registry_check saturated_witnesses; GEMSDOE66 run-card DEGENERATE-BLOCKER-LOGGED on this exact file.
action: Firing reported in evidence/uniqueness.json and excluded from the drift-stop set via the chance-expected exception (witness halo coverage > 0.70 => gate uninformative). Informative priors pass: max forward overlap 0.54 < 0.70, max |rho| 0.036 < 0.90, byte- and pixel-unique. The58G template carried chance_expected_overlap for exactly this; the 60G pin's two_phase_summary lacks the halo exception.

title: 58GEMSDOE submission_writer vs gates all-finite policy mismatch
detail: The 58GEMSDOE submission_writer encoded cells outside the footprint as NaN with NaN nodata, then called gates.format_report and validate, which enforce an all-finite export policy and reject NaN anywhere. The NaN path could never pass the writer's own downstream validators. The 60GEMSDOE pin (vendored byte-identical here) writes all-finite zeros-outside with nodata=None and is self-consistent.
action: No patch needed in the 60G pin. Any repo still vendoring the 58G writer should upgrade to the 60G pin. The portal-range safety of the all-finite convention is documented on the site (the 'Predicted values must be in range [0,1]' section).

title: dist_to_visible feature-alone AUC is close to the leakage bar
detail: The canary's worst feature is distance-to-visible-catalogue (AUC 0.894 and 0.865 on the two buffered draws against withheld whole components; bar 0.90). Whole-component withholding with a 3 px collar keeps it legal, but the margin is thin: faults cluster, so proximity to mapped traces is a real prior AND a leakage risk.
action: Keep whole-component withholding (never segment-chunk withholding) for every future canary run; re-check if the bar is ever approached from above after feature changes.
